q_48707.prompt_mask:
Susan, the new receptionist of the Smithsonian Museum in Washington DC, uses the following three functions to model the daily number of visitors to the museum $@T@$ minutes after the museum has opened.

- $@Q@(@T@)$ - the number of people inside the museum
- $@I@(@T@)$ - the rate at which people enter the museum
- $@L@(@T@)$ - the rate at which people leave the museum

What is the relationship between the three functions above?
q_48707.solution_mask:
The function $@Q@(@T@)$ gives the number of people inside the museum $@T@$ minutes after opening. Then,

$$
@Q@'(@T@) = \dfrac{\textrm{d}@Q@(@T@)}{\textrm{d}@T@} = \dfrac{\textrm{Change in }@Q@}{\textrm{Change in }@T@}.
$$

Thus, $@Q@'(@T@)$ gives the rate at which the number of people inside the museum changes $@T@$ minutes after opening.

In addition, we can compute the rate of change of the number of people inside the museum at time $@T@$ by finding the difference between the entry and exit rates at time $@T@.$ That is,

$$
@Q@'(@T@) = @I@(@T@) - @L@(@T@).
$$

- $@Q@(@T@)$ - the number of bacteria in the dish.

- $@R@(@T@)$ - the rate at which the number of bacteria in the dish is increasing.

What is the relationship between $@Q@(@T@)$ and $@R@(@T@)?$
q_72004.solution_mask:
The function $@Q@(@T@)$ gives the number of bacteria inside the dish after $@T@$ hours. Then,

$$
{@Q@}^{′}(@T@)=\frac{\text{d}@Q@(@T@)}{\text{d}@T@}=\frac{\text{Change in }@Q@}{\text{Change in }@T@}.
$$

Thus, ${@Q@}^{′}(@T@)$ gives the rate at which the number of bacteria is increasing at time $@T@$, which is the same as $@R@(@T@).$ Therefore, the relationship between $@Q@(@T@)$ and $@R@(@T@)$ is ${@Q@}^{′}(@T@)=@R@(@T@).$
